cards.translation: ser responsável por; estar no comando de
cards.definition: To have control of or responsibility for something or someone.
cards.example:
- I am in charge of the monthly sales reports and two junior analysts.
Sou responsável pelos relatórios mensais de vendas e por dois analistas juniores.
- Who is in charge of onboarding the new hires?
Quem é responsável por integrar os novos contratados?
- She was in charge of the Brazilian market for six years.
Ela foi responsável pelo mercado brasileiro por seis anos.
cards.note: Use com substantivo ou com -ing: in charge of the reports, in charge of training new people. Sem complemento, o of cai: Who is in charge here? Sinônimo próximo: be responsible for.

cards.definition: To have someone as your direct manager.
cards.example:
- I report to the head of marketing, and we have a quick meeting every Monday.
Reporto-me à chefe de marketing, e temos uma reunião rápida toda segunda.
- After the restructure, the whole team reported to a new director.
Depois da reestruturação, a equipe inteira passou a se reportar a um novo diretor.
- How many people report to you?
Quantas pessoas se reportam a você?
cards.note: I report to the CFO significa que o CFO é meu chefe. Não confunda com escrever um relatório, que é write a report. Passado: reported to.

cards.definition: A person who works with you.
cards.example:
- My colleagues always help me when I have too many tasks at the same time.
Meus colegas sempre me ajudam quando tenho tarefas demais ao mesmo tempo.
- I share an office with two colleagues from the legal team.
Divido a sala com dois colegas do jurídico.
- A former colleague recommended me for this position.
Um ex-colega me indicou para esta vaga.
cards.note: Cuidado com college (faculdade), que é outra palavra. Colega de escola é classmate. No inglês americano do dia a dia, coworker é igualmente comum.

cards.definition: The amount of work a person or a team has to do.
cards.example:
- My workload gets much heavier at the end of the month, especially in December.
Minha carga de trabalho fica bem mais pesada no fim do mês, principalmente em dezembro.
- We hired an assistant to reduce the team's workload.
Contratamos um assistente para reduzir a carga de trabalho da equipe.
- How do you manage your workload when everything is urgent?
Como você administra sua carga de trabalho quando tudo é urgente?
cards.note: Combina com heavy e light: a heavy workload, a light workload. É uma palavra só, sem espaço, e costuma ficar no singular.

cards.definition: To take care of a person, a problem or a task.
cards.example:
- In this position, I deal with customers from three different countries every day.
Nessa função, lido com clientes de três países diferentes todos os dias.
- Yesterday I dealt with two complaints before lunch.
Ontem lidei com duas reclamações antes do almoço.
- Who deals with invoices while you are on vacation?
Quem cuida das faturas enquanto você está de férias?
cards.note: Serve para pessoas, problemas e tarefas: I deal with complaints. Passado e particípio: dealt with. Não existe “treat with” nesse sentido.

cards.definition: To give someone a job in your company.
cards.example:
- My company is hiring two new analysts because the team is growing fast.
Minha empresa está contratando dois analistas novos porque a equipe cresce rápido.
- They hired her right after the second interview.
Eles a contrataram logo depois da segunda entrevista.
- We need someone with more experience in data, so we will hire externally.
Precisamos de alguém com mais experiência em dados, então vamos contratar fora.
cards.note: O contrário é fire (demitir). Passado: hired. “Contratar alguém” não é contract; como substantivo, a new hire é um novo contratado.

cards.translation: fazer de tudo um pouco; acumular funções
cards.definition: To do many different jobs in the same position.
cards.example:
- In a startup, everyone wears many hats — sales, support and even marketing.
Numa startup, todo mundo faz de tudo um pouco — vendas, suporte e até marketing.
- As an office manager, I wear many hats during the week.
Como gerente do escritório, acumulo funções durante a semana.
- In my first job I wore many hats and learned a lot.
No meu primeiro emprego acumulei funções e aprendi muito.
cards.note: Expressão idiomática: não tem nada a ver com chapéus de verdade. Passado de wear: wore. Ótima em entrevista para descrever funções variadas.

cards.definition: To do your job well when there is stress or very little time.
cards.example:
- I can work under pressure when deadlines are close, but I prefer to plan ahead.
Consigo trabalhar sob pressão quando os prazos apertam, mas prefiro planejar antes.
- The job ad says you must be able to work under pressure.
O anúncio da vaga diz que você precisa saber trabalhar sob pressão.
- During the audit, we had to work under pressure for three weeks.
Durante a auditoria, tivemos que trabalhar sob pressão por três semanas.
cards.note: Clássica de entrevista. A preposição é under, nunca “in pressure”. Aparece muito com can e be able to: I can work under pressure.

cards.definition: To act as if something is true when it is not.
cards.example:
- He pretends to like Monday meetings, but everybody on the team knows the truth.
Ele finge gostar das reuniões de segunda, mas todo mundo da equipe sabe a verdade.
- She pretended not to see the email until Monday.
Ela fingiu não ver o e-mail até segunda.
- Don't pretend you understood the brief; ask again.
Não finja que entendeu o briefing; pergunte de novo.
cards.note: “Pretendo crescer na empresa” não é I pretend — é I intend to ou I plan to. Passado: pretended. Estruturas comuns: pretend to + verbo e pretend that + frase.

cards.definition: The place where you study after high school.
cards.example:
- She studied engineering in college and started working here right after graduation.
Ela estudou engenharia na faculdade e começou a trabalhar aqui logo depois de se formar.
- I went back to college at thirty to change careers.
Voltei para a faculdade aos trinta para mudar de carreira.
- Most of our interns are still in college.
A maioria dos nossos estagiários ainda está na faculdade.
cards.note: “Colégio” do ensino médio é high school. Não confunda com colleague (colega de trabalho). Nos EUA, college e university são quase sinônimos na conversa.

questions.prompt: Which word means the school you attend after high school?
questions.explanation: “College” is a place; “colleague” and “coworker” are people you work with.

questions.prompt: My _____ doubles every December, so I take my vacation in February.
questions.explanation: “Workload” is the amount of work you have to do.

questions.prompt: Eu quero ser responsável pelo novo projeto no ano que vem.
questions.answer: I want to be in charge of the new project next year.|I would like to be in charge of the new project next year.
questions.explanation: “Be in charge of” means to have responsibility for something.

questions.prompt: The CFO is your direct manager. How do you say this at work?
options: I write a report to the CFO.
I report the CFO every week.
I am reported by the CFO.
questions.explanation: “Report to” someone means that person is your manager.

questions.prompt: The team is growing, so we need to _____ two more developers before the launch.
questions.explanation: “Hire” means to give someone a job. The opposite is “fire”.

questions.answer: Can you work under pressure?|Are you able to work under pressure?

questions.prompt: In a small company you do sales, support and marketing yourself. Which sentence describes that?
questions.explanation: “Wear many hats” means you have several different roles.

questions.prompt: The support team has to _____ complaints all day long.
questions.explanation: “Deal with” means to handle a problem, a task or a person.

questions.prompt: Preciso falar com um colega do time de vendas.
questions.answer: I need to talk to a colleague from the sales team.|I need to speak to a colleague from the sales team.
questions.explanation: A “colleague” is a person who works with you.

options: I pretend to apply for the manager position.
She pretends me to finish the report today.
We pretend the meeting for next week.
He pretended to be busy when the boss walked in.
questions.answer: He pretended to be busy when the boss walked in.
questions.explanation: “Pretend” means to fake something; for plans use “intend” or “plan”.
